title: WSJ：Anthropic 7 位创始人 IPO 各套现约 2.5 亿美元并保留控制权
content:
Rohan Paul· @rohanpaul_ai · X·· 4 小时前精选AI 评分79
AI 导读
WSJ 报道，Anthropic 7 位创始人将在 IPO 中各出售约 2.5 亿美元股票，每人保留约 180 亿美元持仓。据公司文件，每人出售近 3.4M 股，发行价区间预计 70 至 78 美元，上市预计下周进行，估值接近 1.3 万亿美元，募资 800 亿美元以上，部分通过包括 Google 在内的私募配售。
推荐理由
原文转述 WSJ 报道并给出招股文件细节，读者可以据此理解 Anthropic IPO 中创始人套现与双重股权控制安排。
正文 · AI 翻译
WSJ：Anthropic的7位创始人将在其IPO中各自出售约2.5亿美元的股票，并各自保留约180亿美元。
根据周二的公司文件，每人都计划以70至78美元的预计区间出售近340万股。
此次上市预计在下周进行，将使Anthropic的估值接近1.3万亿美元，并筹集800亿美元或更多，部分通过向包括Google在内的投资者进行私募配售。
一旦开始交易，每位创始人保留约3.2%的A类股，因此他们合计持有约22%的流通股。
该持股仅附带约11.2%的投票权，然而一个由创始人控制的LLC持有一股F类股，保证他们在大多数股东投票中获得50.1%的投票权
因此，Anthropic股票的公开买家获得了经济利益，却几乎对控制权没有发言权，文件警告称这可能使决策与股东的财务利益相悖。
来源：Rohan Paul · x.com

report.summary: Anthropic's seven co-founders will each sell about $250M of stock in its IPO while keeping roughly $18B stakes and, via a special share class, 50.1% voting control.
report.background: Anthropic was founded in 2021 by a group of former OpenAI researchers, led by CEO Dario Amodei, and has become one of the two or three largest frontier AI labs on the strength of its Claude model family. It has raised tens of billions from strategic backers including Google and Amazon, and has been spending heavily on compute, talent and safety research — costs that make public markets an attractive source of long-term capital. Dual-class share structures are a well-worn path in tech: Google, Meta and Snap all listed with founder-controlled voting rights, letting insiders raise money without ceding direction. A founder cash-out at IPO is also common, giving early principals liquidity after years of illiquid equity. Note that the reported $1.3 trillion valuation and $80B+ raise would be unprecedented in scale, and should be treated as reported figures pending confirmation.
key_points: Scale of the founder sale: each of the seven co-founders plans to sell close to 3.4 million shares at an expected $70–78 range, netting about $250M apiece, according to the filing. Even after selling, each would retain roughly 3.2% of the Class A stock — worth about $18B at the implied valuation — so their economic exposure to Anthropic stays very large.

Two-tier share structure: the founders' Class A holdings add up to about 22% of shares outstanding but carry only about 11.2% of the votes. A founder-controlled LLC holds a single Class F share that guarantees the group 50.1% of votes on most shareholder matters, locking in control regardless of how much stock is sold or diluted over time.

Deal size and backers: the listing is expected next week at a valuation near $1.3 trillion, raising $80B or more, with part of the offering structured as private placements to investors including Google. That would make it one of the largest capital raises in market history and would deepen big-tech entanglement with the lab.

Governance warning in the filing: the prospectus itself cautions that the control arrangement could lead to decisions that diverge from the financial interests of public shareholders — a standard, but pointed, disclosure that buy-side investors will weigh when pricing the deal.
report.impact: For the AI industry, a listing at this scale would reset benchmarks for what frontier labs are worth and give Anthropic a war chest for compute and talent that rivals will have to match — intensifying the capital arms race and pushing other labs toward public markets or mega-rounds. For developers, the more relevant signal is stability: a well-capitalised, founder-controlled Anthropic means the Claude API and model roadmap are unlikely to be driven by quarterly earnings pressure, but pricing and access could still shift as public-market expectations bite. For regular users, the near-term effect is minimal; longer term, a founder-locked structure concentrates decisions about safety policy, model releases and data use in very few hands — with public shareholders holding little formal leverage to object.
report.tools: To follow the deal, watch SEC EDGAR for Anthropic's S-1 and amendments (full-text search for 'Class F' and 'dual-class'), plus Crunchbase or PitchBook for cap-table tracking. For developers wanting portable alternatives to any single vendor, OpenRouter gives one API across Claude, GPT and open models; vLLM and Ollama let you self-host Llama, Mistral or Qwen models; and LMArena plus Artificial Analysis provide independent model comparisons for planning multi-vendor fallbacks.
